Decisions, so there's nothing to ask about:
- Also add a `changelogs/fragments/` bugfix entry. ansible-core expects one on every bugfix PR.
- New files must be tracked (commit them or `git add -N`), or `git diff f7234968d241d7171aadb1e873a67510753f3163` will leave them out. Stage only the files you changed and keep the in-repo `.venv` out of the diff.
- Before you post, run `git apply --check final.patch` on a throwaway `git worktree add --detach <dir> f7234968d241d7171aadb1e873a67510753f3163`.

Post one comment with `final.patch` attached and the output of `python -m pytest test/units/utils/ test/units/vars/` pasted in. Don't change the status and don't @mention me. Your reply wakes me automatically.

The patch isn't posted yet. Dev B's run is still going and their working copy already has the fix, tests and changelog fragment. The issue stays In Progress until I've reviewed `final.patch`.

What I confirmed on my own clone of `f7234968d`:
- **Root cause:** `VarsWithSources` defines none of the union operators. `dict | VWS`, `VWS | dict`, `VWS | VWS` and `VWS |= dict` all raise `TypeError`. So the fix has to add `__or__`, `__ror__` and `__ior__`, not only `__ror__`. Dev B's version adds all three.
- **Baseline:** on the untouched commit, `python -m pytest test/units/utils/ test/units/vars/` gives `3 failed, 318 passed, 2 skipped`. The failures are `test_warning`, `test_warning_no_color` and `test_variable_manager_role_vars_dependencies`.
  - They come from tests leaking state into each other (the `Display` singleton, `test_logger.py`). Each one passes when run alone.
  - With `--forked`, which is how `ansible-test units` runs, the same suite gives `321 passed, 2 skipped`.

Decisions:
- We leave those 3 failures out of this patch because they're unrelated to the bug. The final comment will show both runs: plain (the same 3 failures as the base commit) and `--forked` (all green).
- When testing in a throwaway worktree, set `PYTHONPATH=lib`. The venv installs ansible in editable mode from `~/work/ansible/lib`, so without it pytest silently tests the main checkout instead.

When `final.patch` is posted, I'll apply it to a clean checkout of the base commit, run the test suite plus a set of operator checks, and move the issue to In Review if everything holds.

`final.patch` is attached. It's `git diff f7234968d241d7171aadb1e873a67510753f3163` and touches 4 files. It's also committed on local branch `work` as `948863ac95`.

**Root cause and fix**
`VarsWithSources` is what `VariableManager.get_vars()` returns when `ANSIBLE_DEBUG` is on. It's a `MutableMapping`, not a `dict` subclass, so it had no `|` support in either direction: `dict | VWS`, `VWS | dict` and `VWS | VWS` all raised. The patch adds `__or__`, `__ror__` and `__ior__` to it in `lib/ansible/vars/manager.py`, mirroring `dict`:
- The right operand wins and neither operand is modified. `|=` updates in place, and non-mappings still raise `TypeError`.
- The result is a `VarsWithSources` that keeps the recorded source of every var that wins. A var overridden by a plain dict drops its source, which would otherwise be wrong. The result compares equal to the equivalent dict.

`combine_vars()` is unchanged. It already validates both operands as `MutableMapping` and returns `a | b`, which is what the triage notes require.

**Tests and changelog**
- `test/units/utils/test_vars.py`: 3 `VarsWithSources` cases in `combine_vars_replace_data`: dict | VWS, VWS | dict and VWS | VWS. Each has a conflicting key that the second operand must win.
- `test/units/vars/test_variable_manager.py`: a new `TestVarsWithSources` class with 5 tests covering each operator, source handling, unmodified operands and `TypeError` for non-mappings.
- `changelogs/fragments/varswithsources-dict-union.yml` (`bugfixes`). It has no upstream issue link because I couldn't reach GitHub to confirm the number.

**Verification**
- `git apply --check final.patch` on a throwaway `git worktree add --detach <dir> f7234968d241d7171aadb1e873a67510753f3163` exits 0 with no output. After applying the patch there, the suite gives the same results as below.
- Without the `manager.py` change, the new tests fail: `test_combine_vars_replace` and 4 of the 5 operator tests. With it, they pass.
- End to end: `ansible-playbook` with `ANSIBLE_DEBUG=1` and `add_host` in a loop crashes on the base commit with `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for |: 'VarsWithSources' and 'dict'`. With the patch it completes.

The 3 failures were already there before the patch. On the untouched base commit, the same command fails the same 3 tests (3 failed, 318 passed, 2 skipped). The patch adds 5 passing tests and no new failures. The cause is test isolation: `test/units/utils/display/test_logger.py` deletes every `ansible*` module from `sys.modules`, so later tests run against duplicate module objects. The two `test_warning` tests also share the `Display` singleton, so the repeated warning is suppressed. `ansible-test units` runs each test in a forked process, which hides this; with `--forked` the whole suite passes (326 passed, 2 skipped). I left those tests out of this patch because fixing them is a separate change.

Not in the patch: the NOTE at `lib/ansible/plugins/action/template.py:131` says `|` can't be used with `VarsWithSources`. That's no longer true, but the code there still works.

Status check: the fix, regression tests, changelog fragment and `final.patch` were posted at 02:21 in the implementation thread. The one open point is the review and the move to In Review, which Dev A owns. Their review run started at 02:21 and is still running, so I haven't touched the status.

The patch passed review, so this is the final version and the issue is moving to In Review. I re-attached `final.patch` (the same file Dev B posted above) along with my full test logs, so everything for the merge is in this one comment.

**What I checked on my own clone:**
- **Patch:** `git apply` works cleanly on a fresh checkout of `f7234968d241d7171aadb1e873a67510753f3163`. Running `git diff` against that commit afterwards reproduces the patch byte for byte (sha256 `56fb7f22f85fb65cd47d0119636ffaa6d55a45e6bb4577451ba9e35a16c9d846`).
- **Behavior:** I ran 20 checks of my own on the new operators and on `combine_vars()`, and all pass. They cover:
  - `dict | VWS`, `VWS | dict` and `VWS | VWS`, with the right operand winning on conflicts;
  - a `defaultdict` or `OrderedDict` on the left;
  - `|=` updating in place;
  - non-mappings raising `TypeError`;
  - `combine_vars()` still raising `AnsibleError` for non-mappings, and merge mode unchanged;
  - operands left unmodified, and no per-variable debug output.
- **Regression test:** I ran the new tests without the fix. `test_combine_vars_replace` fails with the exact reported error, `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for |: 'dict' and 'VarsWithSources'`, and so do 4 of the 5 new operator tests. With the fix, all of them pass.
- **Real playbook:** `ansible-playbook` with `ANSIBLE_DEBUG=1` and `add_host` in a loop crashes with the `TypeError` on the base commit. With the patch it runs to the end.
- **Wider suites:** utils, vars, parsing, action and strategy plugins, executor, playbook, template and inventory with `--forked` give 1122 passed and 2 skipped. On the base commit it's 1117, so the difference is exactly the 5 new tests.

All four points are done and the issue is In Review. Nothing is left for us to do.
